sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: curfews, points penalties by level, restriction cards, affidavits, school proof and work zones
Confusable pairs among the GDL curfews, supervision rules and points penalties, followed by continuation facts on restriction cards, affidavits, school proof, fees and teen work-zone safety; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A06
The two curfews differ: a learner permit holder under 18 may not drive from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., while an Intermediate Restricted driver is barred from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. [A06]
Why it matters: group curfews; confusable permit versus restricted curfew.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A06
The age 21 shows up twice: a permit holder needs a licensed driver 21 or older in the front seat, while a restricted driver may carry extra passengers when one passenger is 21 or older with a valid unrestricted license. [A06]
Why it matters: group supervision; confusable supervisor versus passenger exception.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A03
Points penalties depend on the level: on a learner permit, 6 or more points restart a wait of 180 consecutive clean days, while on the Intermediate Restricted License the same points add 90 days to the one-year minimum. [A03]
Why it matters: group penalties; confusable permit versus restricted points penalty.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A06
Moving from the Intermediate Restricted to the Intermediate Unrestricted License costs a $2 application fee after the one-year minimum. [A06]
Why it matters: group fees; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A06
At 18 a driver may pay an $8 duplicate fee for a license without the word Intermediate, or keep the Intermediate license until the end of its five-year renewal cycle. [A06]
Why it matters: group fees; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A03
Learner permit and Intermediate Restricted holders each receive a Restriction Card to carry, explaining their limits and what is needed to advance to the next level. [A03]
Why it matters: group restriction cards; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A04
The Intermediate Unrestricted level carries no driving restrictions, so no restriction card is issued for it. [A04]
Why it matters: group restriction cards; confusable restricted versus unrestricted card.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A04
If the adult cannot come to the Driver Service Center, the teen affidavit can be completed ahead of time and signed in front of a notary public. [A04]
Why it matters: group affidavits; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A04
A grandparent taking on financial responsibility must bring a notarized authorization signed by the parent, step-parent, custodian or guardian. [A04]
Why it matters: group affidavits; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A04
A minor adding another license class, such as a motorcycle, needs the parent or guardian to sign a second teenage affidavit for that class. [A04]
Why it matters: group affidavits; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-R11 | anchor: A04
Over the summer, an SF1010 signed within the last 30 days of the school year is honored until 30 days after the next school year begins. [A04]
Why it matters: group school proof; confusable school-year versus summer validity.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-R12 | anchor: A04
A student at an out-of-state school, or at an approved private or church school without SF1010 forms, brings a letter on official school letterhead from the principal or headmaster confirming the student is not truant. [A04]
Why it matters: group school proof; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-R13 | anchor: A04
A home-schooled applicant brings a letter from the local director of schools confirming the annual notice of intent to home school, plus Form SF-1193 signed by a parent or guardian. [A04]
Why it matters: group school proof; difficulty high.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-R14 | anchor: A05
Most work zone crashes are rear-end collisions, so teens are told not to tailgate and to slow to the posted work-zone limit. [A05]
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-R15 | anchor: A05
In a work zone, merge early, obey the flaggers, avoid lane changes unless directed, and switch on headlights before entering. [A05]
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-R16 | anchor: A07
The GDL review table shows a learner permit issued for 12 months, with a fee of $10.50 for any applicant under 18. [A07]
Why it matters: group fees; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0034]
